implemented_requirements.evidence: The board is created with `b = [[0] * 9 for _ in range(9)]` and all loops iterate over range(9).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Each row, column, and 3x3 subgrid must contain the digits 1 through 9 exactly once
implemented_requirements.evidence: Function `ok` checks row, column and sub‑grid for duplicates; `conflicts` detects any rule violations; `done` confirms the board is full and conflict‑free.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Allow the player to input values for specific cells
implemented_requirements.evidence: In `main`, user input of three numbers `row col value` is parsed and assigned with `puzzle[r - 1][c - 1] = v`.
Command `check` recomputes `conflicts(puzzle)` and prints the coordinates of mistakes; also automatic display of mistakes each turn.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Confirm when the puzzle is completed
implemented_requirements.evidence: `done(puzzle)` returns true only when the board is full and has no conflicts; when true the program prints "Congratulations! Puzzle completed correctly!".

The code is self‑contained, uses only the Python standard library, and is highly likely to run correctly, satisfying all core requirements.
